newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador natives double ransom for two foreign hostages.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador natives double ransom for two foreign hostages.

text.p: A group of native Ecuadorans said on Thursday it had doubled its ransom demand to $2 million for the release of two oil company workers, one British and the other American, who it is holding hostage.

"We have arrived at $2 million because $1 million is for one organization and the other half for another," indigenous Ashuar leader Sergio Gualinga said in a radio interview. Until Wednesday the group had been asking for ransom of $1 million.

Briton Victor Morley Read and American Mark Thurber have been held hostage by the native group since Saturday, after they entered the Sahime territory without the permission of the Ashuar who control the area.

The hostages were studying the environmental impact on the Amazon jungle region before planned oil production by the Argentine oil company Compania General de Combustibles (CGC) goes ahead. They were contracted out to CGC by U.S. firm Walsh.
The Ashuar are demanding the money as compensation for what they consider to be the theft of ecological information that they claim is exclusively theirs.
The Ashuar protest the exploitation of oil in their area as a threat to "the last reserve of the tropical forest."

"We understand the environmental concerns of the Ashuar. The taking of hostages, nevertheless, is a completely unacceptable form of protest. This kind of act puts a cloud of doubt over all the legitimate complaints of the Ashuar people," the U.S. Embassy in Ecuador said in a statement.
Members of the native group were to meet representatives from CGC later on Thursday after negotiations on Wednesday ended in a stalemate.
